L_CANCEL_SETUP_B:
the new wallet you just made will be lost.
you would have to start over from the menu.
L_FAIL_SETUP_B: nothing was saved. start again from the menu.
L_FAIL_OPEN_B: something went wrong. try again from the menu.
L_WARN_T: YOUR PASSPHRASE IS PART OF THE WALLET
L_WARN_B:
your recovery words + passphrase derive this wallet.
a non-empty passphrase changes which wallet the words
derive. protect both.

a strong passphrase can protect this wallet if the words
are exposed; a weak one can be guessed offline.

NOTHING can recover a lost passphrase. every entry is
valid, so a typo opens another wallet with no error.
recognize yours by its fingerprint:
L_FP_NOTE: your passphrase always opens the wallet with this code
L_FP_NOTE2: not the code you wrote down?  go back and retype your passphrase
L_WEAK_ACK: WEAK PASSPHRASE. TAP OK AGAIN TO USE IT ANYWAY
L_PPINTRO_B:
your recovery words and passphrase together derive this
wallet. the passphrase is typed fresh at every login and
never stored, not even on this device.

with no passphrase, the words derive the base wallet,
which may also contain funds.

make the passphrase strong and back it up separately
from the words. nobody can reset it. if someone finds
your words, they can test passphrase guesses offline.
W_SETUP_S: there is no wallet on this device yet
W_NEW_NOTE: a brand-new wallet made on this device
W_RESTORE_NOTE: bring back a wallet from its recovery words
W_12_NOTE:
recommended. 128 bits of entropy,
easier to copy and verify.
W_24_NOTE:
256 bits of entropy, but longer to copy.
choose it to match an old wallet.
W_RAND_S:
a wallet is only as safe as how randomly it
was created. the camera provides that.
W_RAND_B:
point the camera at anything messy, like
leaves, gravel, or a shuffled deck of cards.
tap the screen once the bar turns green.

your shot is then MIXED with the chip's own
hardware randomness - neither source alone
decides your words.
W_WRITE_S:
these ordered words are your recovery phrase (seed phrase). paper only, never a photo/file.
words + the same passphrase restore this wallet on a compatible BIP39 signer.
W_PROVE_S:
no peeking. prove your paper has the right words in
the right order. you also need the same passphrase
to restore this wallet.
W_RESTORE_S: type each word, then tap it when it appears
W_VERIFY_S: type each word from your paper; the device only confirms
W_CHECK_S: that is not a valid BIP39 recovery phrase
W_CHECK_B:
a word or its position is wrong. check the whole
phrase against your paper and try again.
W_VOK_S: your written words match this wallet's recovery phrase
W_VOK_B:
your paper matches the recovery phrase. keep it offline
and private. words + the same passphrase restore this
wallet on a compatible BIP39 signer.
W_VBAD_S: as written, your paper would not bring this wallet back
W_VBAD_B:
compare your paper with the words on this device
(WALLET > RECOVERY WORDS), fix the copy, then check
again. nothing changed - your wallet is unaffected.
W_VINTRO_S: prove your written words match this wallet's recovery phrase
W_VINTRO_B:
type your recovery words from the paper. the device
only confirms they match - it never shows your
stored words. but you will be typing them, so do
this where no one can see the screen.

one wrong or missing word means your paper would NOT
bring the wallet back - far better to find out now,
before you trust it with coins.
I_S: the wallet you are logged into right now
I_H_FP_B:
a 32-bit code derived from this wallet's master key.
use it as a quick check, not proof.

matching fingerprints usually mean the same master
key, but rare collisions exist. a paired app should
show the same code.
I_H_TYPE_B:
the type of address this wallet generates. Native
SegWit (bc1...) is the modern kind with the lowest fees.

the m/... line is the derivation path: the standard
route used to derive this account's keys. apps use it
to find the same addresses this device does.
I_H_PAIR_B:
an online app that watches this wallet using only a
public key - it cannot sign or authorize a spend by
itself. it just sees balances, builds and broadcasts.

DESKTOP shares a descriptor (Sparrow-style), MOBILE a
zpub (BlueWallet-style) - same wallet, two dialects.
'watch-only' is correct: every spend signs HERE.
I_H_ADDR_B:
address #0, shown so you can recognize this wallet
at a glance. a paired app should show exactly this
same address first.

addresses are safe to share: they can receive coins,
they can never spend them.
I_PAIR_S: show this QR to the app that will watch this wallet
I_NOTE_BW:
phone apps that read a key (zpub): BlueWallet
(add wallet > import > scan), Nunchuk, Ibis...
the app may say 'watch-only' - correct: it only
watches + broadcasts. every send signs HERE.
I_NOTE_SPARROW:
computer apps that read a descriptor: Sparrow
(File > New Wallet > Airgapped Hardware Wallet),
Specter, Nunchuk, Fully Noded...
I_PROVE:
then prove it: RECEIVE > VERIFY - scan the
app's first address to confirm it's yours.
first time? practice with a tiny send first.
I_PAIR_BTN_NOTE:
connect the app that watches your balance
and prepares transactions. it cannot sign
or authorize - only this device does.
I_WORDS_BTN_NOTE:
see the words that rebuild this wallet,
or prove your written copy is correct.
I_WORDS_S: copy them onto paper, in order. never a photo, never a file.
I_WARN_S: the words that rebuild this wallet
I_WARN_B:
make sure nobody can see the screen.

these words + your passphrase derive THIS wallet. if the
passphrase is non-empty, words alone derive another wallet.
exposed words let an attacker test passphrase guesses
offline. treat them as critical secrets.

never type them into a phone or computer.
never photograph them. paper only.

this is a STANDARD backup: words + the same passphrase
restore on a compatible BIP39 signer. after an emergency
phone/desktop restore, sweep the coins to a fresh offline
wallet.
G_TESTNET_NOTE:
TESTNET: practice coins with no value.
free from coinfaucet.eu
G_TY_NATIVE_NOTE:
modern, lowest fees. use this
unless an app needs another kind.
G_TY_NESTED_NOTE:
older segwit. only to match a
wallet that needs it.
G_TY_LEGACY_NOTE:
oldest style, highest fees. only to
match a very old wallet.
G_SEPARATE: each network + type is its own separate wallet
G_CREATE_NOTE:
make a fresh wallet, or restore one from
recovery words. this REPLACES the wallet
on here - back up the old words first.
G_WIPE_NOTE:
removes the wallet from this device.
recovery words + the same passphrase restore it.
G_NOERASE_B:
the recovery words may STILL be on this device.
do not sell it or give it away. try the wipe again;
if it keeps failing, treat the device as if it
holds your words.
G_ERASED_B:
the recovery words are gone from this device.
nothing on here can spend from that wallet anymore.

your paper backup + the same passphrase still work:
restore from Settings, or create a brand-new wallet.
R_S: this address was made on the device. trust what you see here, not your computer screen.
R_REUSED:
already used
reusing links your coins
R_VERIFY_NOTE:
VERIFY: scan an address your computer shows
and this device says if it is really yours
R_VS: checked on this device, against this wallet's own keys
R_CHANGE_FMT: change address #%u - your coordinator uses these internally
R_RECV_FMT: receive address #%u - safe to give out or send to
R_NOT_B:
not among this wallet's first 200 receive or change addresses.
it could be another address type or network setting, a different
wallet, or malware swapping addresses on your computer.
do not send to it until you know whose it is.
N_S: show the coordinator's QR to the camera
N_TAP_CANCEL: tap the top-left corner to cancel
N_RETRY: tap the top-left corner to go back and retry
S_GET_TX: get the transaction from your coordinator
S_POINT_CAM:
point the camera at the QR your
coordinator wallet shows
S_OR_LOAD: or load a .psbt file saved on a card
S_COORD_B:
the wallet app on your computer or phone (Sparrow, for
example). it watches your balance and builds each
transaction, but cannot sign it on its own.

it shows the tx as a QR (often moving - hold steady).
this device signs, then shows a QR back to the app.
S_SD_SUB: move the transaction by SD card
S_INSERT_CARD: insert a card holding the PSBT file your coordinator saved
S_SPARROW_SAVE: in Sparrow Wallet: save the transaction as a PSBT file onto the card
S_CHOOSE_FILE: choose the transaction file to verify
S_READ_FAIL: could not read that file (too big or unreadable)
S_NOT_PSBT: that file is not a valid PSBT
S_SCAN_NOT_PSBT: the scanned data is not a valid PSBT
S_CHANGE_TAG: change back to you, verified here
S_SP_NOTE: address computed on this device, re-checked by your coordinator
S_WONT_SIGN: this device will not sign it
S_WHY_HIGHFEE:
HIGH FEE: the fee is a big share of what you send.
check the rate is what you meant to pay.
S_WHY_TINYCH:
TINY CHANGE: this leaves a very small change coin.
it fragments your balance and can be used to track
you across payments.
S_WHY_FOOT:
unsure? go BACK, then in your coordinator
(Sparrow / BlueWallet) freeze or label the coin
and rebuild the transaction without it.
S_RBF_B_ON:
RBF = Replace-By-Fee. if this transaction gets stuck
unconfirmed, it can be re-sent with a higher fee to
speed it up. a normal, standard setting - most
wallets turn it on by default.

it does NOT change where your coins go, only whether
the fee can be bumped later.
S_RBF_B_OFF:
this transaction is final: it cannot be re-sent with a
higher fee later (the opposite of RBF). if it gets
stuck, you wait it out.

it does NOT change where your coins go.
S_DONE_SD_SUB: signed successfully. take this card to your coordinator to broadcast
S_SAVED_NOTE: saved to the card. this device never touched the network
S_FAIL_SIGN: the transaction could not be signed
S_FAIL_SD_WRITE: could not write to the SD card
S_QR_FAIL_ENC: could not encode the signed transaction
S_QR_SUB: signed successfully. scan this with your coordinator to broadcast
S_QR_LOOP: it keeps looping, so hold your phone steady
S_NO_NETWORK: this device never touched the network
S_EZ_NOTE:
phone won't catch it? bigger dots,
slower loop - same transaction
S_D_MANYIN_FMT:
THIS TRANSACTION HAS %u INPUTS
showing %u here - all are verified as yours
S_D_TXID_SAME: your coordinator shows this same id
S_D_LT_NONZERO: locktime: earliest block it can confirm
S_D_SIGHASH:
sighash ALL: signatures cover every
amount and destination above
S_D_RBF_ON:
replaceable (RBF): the fee can be
bumped after broadcast
P_PREV_MISMATCH: input's previous transaction does not match
P_LEGACY_PREV: legacy input needs its full previous transaction
P_TOO_MANY_VERIFY: too many outputs to verify safely
P_SP_NEED_V2: silent payment needs a v2 transaction
P_SP_RECEIVE: cannot spend silent payment coins (send only)
P_SP_INPUTS: silent payments need native segwit inputs
P_SP_DERIVE: could not build the silent payment safely
H_FP_CARD_B:
a 32-bit code derived from THIS wallet's master key.
use it as a quick check, not proof.

matching fingerprints usually mean the same master
key, but rare collisions exist. your app and SIGN
should show the same code.
